A client wants rights to everything we create, including rejected concepts and our internal tools. Do we sign?

An example AI answer

Yes, if the fee covers the full rights transfer and the terms are clear.

How a design studio founder would decide

Rights to everything delivered and paid for, yes; rejected concepts and the studio's own tools and templates stay ours.

An A/B test says smaller, lighter legal text under the signup button lifts signups 4%. Should we ship it?

A 4% lift is worth taking. Ship it, and keep the text readable.

How a design director would decide

Keep the legal text at body size and full contrast, and give up the 4 percent.

We have $2M in the bank and 11 months of runway. Is now the time for a $200k brand campaign?

Yes. Brand takes time to build, so start now and set goals you can track.

How a head of growth would decide

No. With under twelve months of runway, only spend that returns cash inside the quarter.

A competitor had an outage today and our product stayed up. Should we post about it?

Yes, tastefully: highlight your uptime without naming them.

How a head of social media would decide

No. Say nothing about their outage. If users of theirs come asking, answer them one to one.

## Why not just write a prompt?

- Custom instructions that start “Act as a senior…”

- A paragraph of context, pasted into every new chat.

- One more correction, when it confidently suggests something you would never do.

A job title tells your AI who to imitate. Your decisions show it what you actually weigh, where you stop, and why.

A Decision Model is a record of what one professional actually decided, and why. It shows how they weigh trade-offs, where they stop, and what won when goals collided. Your AI applies it to new situations and reads the expert’s new version the next time it asks.
